newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik plant to produce 30-40 T antimony in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Tajik plant to produce 30-40 T antimony in 1996.

text.p: Tajikistan's Isfarinsky Hydrometallurgical Plant has begun antimony production with output seen at 30-40 tonnes for 1996, a company official said on Tuesday.
The plant has produced 10 tonnes since August, and annual production is planned at around 100-150 tonnes a year, director, Kutbiddin Eshonov, told Reuters.
Located in the north of the remote Central Asian nation, the plant uses mercury-antimony concentrates mined in the mountains of central Tajikistan.
In Soviet times, concentrates were refined at the Kadamzhai Antimony Works in the neighbouring republic of Kyrgyzstan.
"Our aim is to work with finished products, not trade with semi-finished ones," Eshonov said.
He said the plant needed at least $3 million to bring it up to full capacity of 200-250 tonnes a year, but potential investors were put off by instability in the war-torn country.
The former Soviet republic has suffered a bloody four-year civil war.
